body: The live consumer of jwt-decode, which had no test of its own.

author: reek
body: While the decoder returned every claim empty, this function answered JwtOk and built an ExternalIdentity whose subject and email were the empty string, for every token from every provider.

author: reek
body: bridge-authenticate answers Maybe now, so the three cases below are genuinely different answers rather than three records that differ only in how empty they are. The refusals are the point: an unreadable token used to produce an identity carrying the provider's real access and refresh tokens, and a token with no sub used to produce one whose key was "<provider>:" and therefore collided with every other such login.

author: reek
body: The good token is the control. Without it the two refusals would be evidence that this function always says no, which is exactly as useless as always saying yes.

author: reek
body: A refused login must leave the store untouched. Adding the Maybe to the signature is only worth something if nothing downstream can still reach an identity that was never authenticated, and the count is what says so.
